Abstract-only grading, and the study period contains an apparent date error (September 2026)."},"practical_usefulness":{"score":2,"justification":"Mainly of academic interest. It reinforces looking for lip pits and submucous clefts, but offers no actionable change in management."},"summary":"Retrospective review of 5528 cleft patients at one Japanese dental hospital identified 22 with Van der Woude syndrome. Lower lip pits were present in 86.4%, and cleft lip and palate was the most common cleft type (59.1%). All 19 overt clefts were complete, and 13.6% had submucous cleft palate. 59.1% had no documented family history.","why_it_matters":"It reminds surgeons to look for lip pits and submucous cleft palate in cleft patients, including those with no family history, to support diagnosis and genetic counselling."}
